question.problem:
Find the inverse of the elementary matrix 
$N=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{12}\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
We write down $N$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply an elementary row operation that transforms the left matrix into the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}[N\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{12} & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{2}:=12{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 12\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse is obtained on the right-hand side of our big matrix after the transformation. Therefore, 

$$
{N}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 12\end{aligned}].
$$
